title: Pixel Grid Sketchpad
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Framebuffer
OLED
Pixel Coordinates
Bit Operations
SSD1306
description: Draw on a 128 by 64 OLED pixel grid and see which of the 1,024 framebuffer bytes and which bit stores each pixel.

learningObjectives: Apply x and y coordinates to locate pixels on a 128 by 64 display
Calculate the byte index and bit for any pixel using index = x + (y // 8) * 128 and bit = y % 8
Analyze why one byte stores a vertical strip of 8 pixels
prerequisites: Screen coordinates with (0, 0) at the top-left (Chapter 10)

keyQuestions: How many bytes does a 128-pixel horizontal line touch?
Why does the buffer need only 1,024 bytes for 8,192 pixels?
commonMisconceptions: Each pixel is one byte (each pixel is one bit)
Bytes run across rows like text (on the SSD1306 they run down 8-pixel columns)
assessmentOpportunities: The student calculates index and bit for a given pixel without the tool.
The student explains why a horizontal line touches 1 byte per column while a vertical 8-pixel strip fits in one byte.
The student reads (x, y) correctly with y growing downward.
